purpose.summary: Arrange elements with tokenised spacing — the only sanctioned way to put gaps between things
useWhen: Two or more elements need space between them: a toolbar, a form, a card's contents, a page section
You would otherwise reach for a raw flex or grid utility class plus a hand-picked gap
You want spacing that moves with the token scale rather than a number frozen into a class name
You need a row (Layout.Horizontal) or a column (Layout.Vertical) — the two cases that cover most UI
doNotUseWhen: A component already arranges its own children — ButtonGroup, ButtonLayout, Table, Card and the form primitives own their internal spacing, and wrapping their slots in a Layout fights them
A single element needs margin from its neighbour — put the gap on the shared parent instead, so it cannot drift out of step
You need true positioning (absolute, sticky, fixed) or a scroll container — Layout only emits display, direction, alignment and gap
You are spacing text inside a paragraph or list — that is typography's line-height and margin, not a layout gap

codeOnly.name: direction
codeOnly.notes: Layout.Flex only. Layout.Horizontal and Layout.Vertical fix it to row and column respectively and ignore anything you pass. Prefer Horizontal/Vertical over Flex with an explicit direction — they read better and carry a gap default. A designer expresses this as auto-layout direction on an ordinary frame.

codeOnly.name: align
codeOnly.notes: Cross-axis alignment (align-items), on both Flex and Grid. With no value the browser default (stretch) applies, which is usually what a column wants and rarely what a row of mixed-height items wants — pass 'center' for a row of a label and a control.

codeOnly.name: justify
codeOnly.notes: Main-axis distribution (justify-content), on both Flex and Grid. There is no 'around' or 'evenly' — if you need those, the arrangement is probably a grid with sized tracks.

codeOnly.name: wrap
codeOnly.notes: Layout.Flex, Horizontal and Vertical only. Unset means the browser default of nowrap, so a row of chips or tags that can overflow needs an explicit wrap — this is the single most common omission.

codeOnly.name: gap
codeOnly.notes: Space on both axes, from the layout token scale. Available on every namespace member. Layout.Horizontal and Layout.Vertical default it to 'md'; Layout.Flex and Layout.Grid have no default at all and render flush unless you pass one (see LYT-001).

codeOnly.name: gapX
codeOnly.notes: Horizontal gap only (column-gap). Use with gapY for a wrapping row or a grid that needs different spacing per axis. Passing gap as well applies both classes and the result depends on stylesheet order — pass gapX/gapY or gap, not both (see LYT-002).

codeOnly.name: gapY
codeOnly.notes: Vertical gap only (row-gap). The one that matters on a wrapping row: without it, wrapped lines sit flush against each other.

codeOnly.name: flow
codeOnly.notes: Layout.Grid only (grid-auto-flow). Applied as an inline style, not a class, because Tailwind cannot emit a utility for a value only known at runtime.

codeOnly.name: grow
codeOnly.notes: Layout.Flex, Horizontal and Vertical only. Sets flex-grow on the container itself, so it fills its own parent — it does not make the children grow. For that, put the grow on the child, or make it a Grid with sized tracks.

codeOnly.name: columns
codeOnly.notes: Layout.Grid only. A number becomes that many equal columns; a string is passed straight through as grid-template-columns ('1fr 2fr', 'repeat(auto-fit, minmax(12rem, 1fr))'). Applied as an inline style because the value is runtime-known. The raw-string form is an escape hatch, not a token-governed value — keep any lengths in it to rem or fr, never px.

codeOnly.name: rows
codeOnly.notes: Layout.Grid only, the grid-template-rows equivalent of columns, with the same inline-style mechanics and the same caution about raw lengths.

codeOnly.name: className
codeOnly.notes: Merged through cn() after the variant classes. This is where positioning, sizing, overflow and borders go, since Layout emits none of them. Do not put a gap or a padding here — gap has a prop, and padding belongs to the component being laid out.

codeOnly.name: children
codeOnly.notes: The elements being arranged. Layout renders a plain div wrapper and does not inspect, filter or clone them.

composition.notes: Anything. Layout is a transparent wrapper — it adds a div with display, alignment and gap classes and nothing else. A Layout with one child only makes sense for its grow or alignment behaviour.

keyboardSupport: None. Layout renders a plain div and is not focusable, so it adds nothing to the tab order
accessibility.notes: Layout is presentational and contributes no semantics. Two consequences worth stating: visual order comes from direction, so 'row-reverse' and 'column-reverse' make the reading order disagree with the DOM order, which is what a screen reader and the tab sequence follow — avoid them for anything interactive. And Layout emits no landmark, list or group semantics, so a toolbar, navigation region or list needs the right element or role around it; a Layout is not a substitute.

governance.tokenStatus: Gap refs record the layout alias layer the gap-cn-* utilities actually point at (--cn-layout-*), not the spacing primitives those aliases resolve to — consistent with the audit-by-alias rule. gap='none' is the one exception: it emits gap-0, which is the spacing.0 primitive directly. Layout emits no colour, radius, border or typography tokens of any kind

knownGaps: LYT-001: gap defaults are inconsistent across the namespace. Layout.Horizontal and Layout.Vertical default gap to 'md'; Layout.Flex and Layout.Grid have no gap default and render flush. Swapping Horizontal for Flex with direction='row' silently removes all spacing
LYT-002: gap and gapX/gapY are not mutually exclusive in the type. Passing both emits both class sets and the outcome depends on stylesheet order rather than on anything the call site can see

LYT-003: columns, rows and flow are applied as inline styles because Tailwind cannot generate utilities for runtime values. They therefore win over any className, cannot be overridden by a consumer's class, and sit outside the token system — columns='320px 1fr' is accepted with no warning

LYT-004: no Figma component and no Code Connect file. Arrangement is expressed as auto-layout on a plain frame, so design and code cannot be checked against each other, and a designer's gap choice reaches code only by hand
LYT-005: Layout emits no class of its own, so there is no cn-layout hook for a consumer to target in a stylesheet or for a tool to find in the built CSS
LYT-006: direction 'row-reverse' and 'column-reverse' decouple visual order from DOM order, and nothing in the API warns about it
LYT-007: grow is a container-level flex-grow and is frequently mistaken for a child-level one. There is no prop for making children grow

LYT-008: the JSDoc gap table in the source maps each size straight to a --cn-spacing-* value, skipping the --cn-layout-* alias the utilities actually reference. The resolved values are correct today but the table will go stale if the alias layer is retargeted
